c: Profusione D'Amore fires flowers away from the character's walking direction that bounce off of walls and obstacles, but pierce through an unlimited number of enemies. As they reach the end of their

, they slow down and shed petals in a small X shape, dealing additional damage to nearby enemies. Profusione D'Amore starts a petal effect after a normal attack, then sends out water waves with flowers across the entire screen on the next attack. It deals around four and a half times the damage compared to the normal flowers. These waves pick a random point to start propagating.
, and its Interval is removed spawning all the flowers at once.
increases its overall spawn rate when moving, when the character stops it initiates the default
. Profusione D'Amore ignores Projectile Speed bonuses outside of its level ups.

Profusione D'Amore has a 0.3 second Hitbox Delay, meaning that the same enemy cannot be hit more often than every 0.3 seconds by the same flower. However, because all active delays are reset simultaneously as soon as any one elapses, some enemies may get hit more often.
Profusione D'Amore gains a 66%[Verify] chance to generate a
Little Heart when an enemy is defeated. This chance is unaffected by

It causes O'Sole Meeo to visually transform into a dancing sun god surrounded by flowers. If a character other than O'Sole gets the weapon, a translucent, transformed O'Sole appears behind the character.
- Allows Profusione D'Amore's Little Hearts to heal 2 points of health and trigger a pulse dealing the same amount of damage.
- Allows the flowers to explode when they expire. The explosions also have the same chance to generate Little Hearts. Damage is based on

Profusione D'Amore is a reference to the 2006 action-adventure game
, in which a white wolf goddess and main protagonist
leaves grass and flowers behind her as she walks and runs.
One of the objectives of the game is to restore the
to rid of the curse that plagues the land of Nippon, clearing the way for that area to move forward in the game. It is accompanied by a

where the leaves of the Guardian Sapling spread out, and the curse is lifted with a pulse of green energy spreading out across the area. As the energy moves across the land, it is rejuvenated as flowers blooms on the pulse while body of water like rivers or seas are cleared as curved water waves splashes out. The petals spreading out and both aspects of the recovery are referenced with the two stages of petals covering the full screen and the screen clear attack animation.
Profusione D'Amore literally translates to "Profusion of Love" in Italian, a reference to the song "
